text: On a morning this cold, the river still hasn’t frozen; it breathes white steam.
say: On a morning this cold, the river hasn't frozen; it breathes white steam.
asr: On a morning this cold, the river hasn't frozen; it breathes white steam.

text: This is a wetland in eastern Hokkaido.
Asleep, standing in the water: red-crowned cranes.
asr: A sleep, standing in the water, red-crowned cranes.

text: Long ago, as the wetlands were cleared field by field, they nearly lost their home for good.
At daybreak they fly in flocks to a field scattered with corn, just for them.
say: At daybreak, they fly in flocks to a field scattered with corn, just for them.

text: Think back to the winter of 1952: in all of Hokkaido, only 33 cranes were found.
say: The winter of nineteen fifty-two: in all of Hokkaido, only thirty-three cranes were found.
asr: The winter of 1952, in all of Hokkaido, only 33 cranes were found.

text: That was the year local people decided to feed them through the winter.
And so, year after year, there were more of them.

say: By twenty twenty-five the count reached one thousand nine hundred twenty-seven.

text: Their status finally eased, from Vulnerable to Near Threatened.
No longer counted as endangered, these spirits of the snow still need people to look after them.
